evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:190-231 — refreshToken() wraps the whole refresh in one try/catch and calls logout() on ANY failure, including a rejected fetch() (offline/timeout/DNS) or 5xx, not only a 401/invalid-refresh-token response. logout() (lines 155-188) deletes access/refresh tokens + user + tenant and runs resetLocalData(), which purges the offline mutation queue (QUEUE_KEY) and cached responses.

Callers: cold-start initialize() (lines ~338-365) and authenticateWithBiometric() (lines ~290-300) both refresh when the stored access token is expired. A user who opens the app offline (e.g. in a basement/garage, the exact offline-first use case) with an expired access token is therefore force-logged-out and loses queued offline writes (faults, etc.) even though the refresh token is still valid. Fix: only logout on a definitive auth rejection (401/400 from /auth/refresh); on network error/5xx keep tokens and queue, restore session in a degraded offline state and retry refresh later.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/utils/session.ts:113-117 — buildSessionUser trusts an embedded `data.user` via `{ ...embedded } as unknown as SessionUser` without validating fields or passing role through toAppRole(). A server-side fine-grained role (e.g. 'org_admin', 'property_manager') would be stored verbatim in SecureStore USER_KEY and surface in state.user.role (ProfileScreen.tsx:120) outside the AppRole union; missing firstName/lastName would be undefined. The claims-derived path (lines 120-132) normalises correctly, so the two paths diverge. Fix: build the user field-by-field from embedded values with str() and toAppRole(embedded.role).
